records.name: Omega Omega Chapter, Alpha Kappa Alpha Sorority
records.summary: A Philadelphia alumnae chapter of Alpha Kappa Alpha, chartered in 1926. Its foundation gives scholarships and grants, and the chapter runs public programs such as health fairs and voter events.
records.what_you_do: Scholarships go to high school seniors and college students, and the application is linked from the chapter's About Us page. A yearly Day of Sharing gives community grants and scholarships. Members serve on chapter committees, and joining is a separate process.

schedule.text: The site lists no regular meeting. Public events and the scholarship application are posted as they come up.

locations.label: Philadelphia (no meeting address on the site)

first_step.how: Apply for a chapter scholarship if you are a student, or attend a public event posted on the site and ask how to join through the Contact Us page.
first_step.basis: Membership steps are not on the site, so the way in is unclear. Public events are only part of what the chapter does.

records.notes: The site advertises a centennial anniversary gala with ticketing, but shows no date for it. The newest explicit dated item is a 2024 photo caption (year only), so status is probably_active. Footer address and email belong to the website developer and are not recorded. Leadership not verified.

records.name: Philadelphia Alumnae Chapter, Delta Sigma Theta Sorority
records.summary: The Philadelphia alumnae chapter of Delta Sigma Theta, with about 700 members. It works on education, health, economic development and civic life in the city, and it opens some of its events to the public.
records.what_you_do: Public events have included a voter forum, a shredding and electronics disposal drive, health and cybersecurity webinars, and a concert. Some events take registration. Members work through chapter programs in education, health and emergency response, and some events are for members only.

schedule.text: Events are posted on the chapter site as they come up, for example a fundraiser on Thursday, October 15.

first_step.how: Attend a public event listed on the chapter site, such as a voter forum or a community drive, then use the Prospective Membership page to ask about joining.
first_step.basis: Some events are open to the public, but joining goes through a prospective membership process that the site does not spell out.

records.notes: Event dates on the site show weekday and day but no year. The year 2026 is inferred from the weekday (October 15, 2026 is a Thursday). Members-only items such as a walking challenge are not public. The chapter's contact form is the only contact shown on the site.

records.name: Quaker City Alumnae Chapter, Delta Sigma Theta Sorority
records.summary: A Philadelphia alumnae chapter of Delta Sigma Theta, chartered in 1976. It serves the city through education, health, emergency preparedness and social action, and some of its events are open to the public.
records.what_you_do: Public-facing events include a children's coat drive, a fire safety workshop and a community walk. The chapter lists program areas in arts, economic development, education, emergency response, health, international awareness and social action. Joining goes through the national sorority's membership center.

schedule.text: Events are posted with dates on the chapter site. A 50th anniversary gala and a fire safety workshop are both listed for October.

first_step.how: Watch the chapter site for open events such as the coat drive or the fire safety workshop, and email info@dstquakercity.org to ask about membership.
first_step.basis: Some events are public, but membership runs through the national sorority's membership center, so the steps to join are not on the chapter site.

records.notes: Event dates on the site have no year. The year 2026 is inferred from the chapter's 1976 charter and a 50th anniversary gala listed for October 17. The national membership center was not read.

records.name: Philadelphia Alumni Chapter, Kappa Alpha Psi Fraternity
records.summary: The Philadelphia alumni chapter of Kappa Alpha Psi. It runs the Achievement Academy, a youth mentoring program, and funds scholarships through its Achievement Foundation. The chapter is based at the Achievement Center in Germantown.
records.what_you_do: The Achievement Academy works with young people on daily living skills, wellbeing, college exposure and budgeting. Guide Right is a mentoring program linked to a college tour. The Achievement Center can be booked for events through a request form. General chapter meetings are for the fraternity's brothers.

schedule.text: General chapter meeting on the third Wednesday of each month at the Achievement Center, doors open at 5:45 pm. The page invites the fraternity's brothers to attend.

first_step.how: Call (215) 848-4227 or email Info@PhillyKappas.org to ask about the Achievement Academy, or about joining if you are a Kappa brother.
first_step.basis: The site speaks to brothers of the fraternity, and the sign-up steps for the youth program are not on the page.

records.notes: The home page lists a 2026 HBCU Classic Tailgate dated October 30, 2026. The posting date is not shown, so the status rests on that listing. Youth enrollment for the Achievement Academy is on another site (phillykappaskare.org) that was not read. The dues page points to a payment site that was not used.

records.name: Rho Chapter, Alpha Phi Alpha Fraternity
records.summary: The Philadelphia chapter of Alpha Phi Alpha, a men's fraternity. It meets monthly and lists national, special and local service programs, though the site does not describe them.
records.what_you_do: Members meet on the first Monday of the month. The site lists national, special and local programs without describing them, and it promotes a fundraising ball dated November 21, 2026.

schedule.text: Chapter meetings on the first Monday of each month, as the chapter's site says.

locations.label: Meeting site: Historic African Episcopal Church of St. Thomas on Lancaster Avenue

first_step.how: Use the chapter's website contact details to ask how a man joins.
first_step.basis: The fraternity's membership steps are not listed on the site.

records.notes: The status rests on a ball listed for November 21, 2026. The posting date is not shown. The email comes from the city's partner list, not from the chapter site. The city list also names two other Alpha Phi Alpha Philadelphia chapters, recorded as leads.

records.name: Zeta Iota Iota Chapter, Omega Psi Phi Fraternity
records.summary: A Philadelphia chapter of Omega Psi Phi that runs youth education work, an HBCU college tour and health and community action projects. Its Epic Day Party is open to the public and raises money for the chapter's foundation and community causes.
records.what_you_do: The chapter runs youth education and development work, a talent competition for young people, a college tour for HBCUs, and health and social action projects. The Epic Day Party is open to the public. The site does not say how volunteers take part or how a man joins.

schedule.text: The site has a calendar of chapter activities, but the events on the pages we read had no dates.

locations.label: Mailing address: P.O. Box 28967, Philadelphia, PA 19151

first_step.how: Go to an open event listed on the chapter site, such as the Epic Day Party, then email the chapter to ask about joining.
first_step.basis: A public party is open, but the steps to join are not explained, so the way in is unclear.

records.notes: The site has no dated items, so status rests on a working site. The footer copyright range is not used as evidence. The city partner list gives a different contact for this chapter, which is not recorded.

records.name: Beta Delta Zeta Chapter, Zeta Phi Beta Sorority
records.summary: A Philadelphia area chapter of Zeta Phi Beta, serving the area since 1944. It runs fundraisers for health and community causes, including a St. Jude walk team, a bowling party and a supply drive.
records.what_you_do: Events labeled 2026 on the page include a St. Jude Walk team, a bingo afternoon, a bowling party, a March for Babies fundraiser, a period supply drive and a restoration fundraiser for the sorority's founder's house. Ticketed events use online ticket pages. The page does not say how a woman joins.

schedule.text: The St. Jude Walk is held in September. Other events are labeled with a year (2026) but no month.

first_step.how: Join a public fundraiser such as the St. Jude Walk team page, and use the chapter's links to ask about membership.
first_step.basis: Fundraisers invite supporters, but the page does not say how a woman joins.

records.notes: The link page is an aggregator, and the chapter's own website was not read separately. Its events are labeled 2026 with no month, so status is active on the year alone. The national sorority site was not read.

records.name: Penn Towne Chapter, The Links, Incorporated
records.summary: A Philadelphia area chapter of The Links, a national service organization for women, founded in 1975. It offers scholarships and mentoring and holds programs in the arts, sciences, education and civic engagement.
records.what_you_do: The chapter gives scholarships, runs mentoring initiatives, and holds workshops, service projects and fundraisers. The site does not say which of these are open to volunteers or the public, or how to join.

schedule.text: The site lists no dated events.

locations.label: Philadelphia area (the site names no neighborhoods)

first_step.how: Use the site's Contact link to ask about membership, scholarships or mentoring.
first_step.basis: The site has a contact link and a member login, but no steps for joining.

records.notes: The site has no dated items, so status rests on a working site. Penn Towne is a separate chapter from the Philadelphia Links chapter, which has no website we could find.

records.name: 100 Black Men of Philadelphia
records.summary: A mentoring nonprofit for young people in Philadelphia. It pairs boys in grades 2 to 12 with mentors, runs leadership and financial literacy programs, and offers a college prep group for students heading to Lincoln or Cheyney University.
records.what_you_do: Youth enroll online for the Leadership Academy, the mentorship program and financial literacy classes for grades 7 to 12. The group also runs workshops on professional skills, resumes and mock interviews. The site does not say whether adults can volunteer as mentors.

schedule.text: Programs run through the year. The site says to check its calendar for monthly events, but the calendar was not on the page we read.

first_step.how: Use the Click To Enroll link on the site for a youth program, or call (267) 424-2444 to ask about volunteer mentoring.
first_step.basis: Youth programs have a clear online sign-up open to the public. The steps for adult volunteers are not stated.

records.notes: The leadership and mentorship programs are for boys, per the site. The footer copyright year is not used as evidence. A search result mentioned a parent academy co-hosted with the Coalition of 100 Black Women for Philadelphia parents, but no page we could read confirmed it, so it is not recorded. A news item from search gives a chapter president, undated, so it is not recorded.

records.name: Philadelphia Chapter, Jack and Jill of America
records.summary: The founding chapter of Jack and Jill of America, a club of mothers that organizes activities for children from age 2 through 19 in leadership, culture and education.
records.what_you_do: Mothers in the chapter plan activities for children with a focus on leadership, civic involvement and service. The chapter's own pages could not be read, so its public programs and join steps are not listed here.

first_step.how: Email the chapter to ask about the children's programs and how mothers join.
first_step.basis: Membership is for mothers, and the chapter's own pages could not be read, so the steps to join are unclear.

records.notes: The chapter's own page and the national site returned HTTP 403 to every fetch, so this record relies on a search summary of the chapter history and the city's partner list. The newest dated item found is a March 2019 gala, which is not enough to call the chapter active, so status is unknown. Verify with the chapter before relying on the join steps.

notes: Used all 8 WebSearch calls (budget exhausted). About 42 WebFetch calls. Records: 14, verdicts 10 publish and 4 out_of_area. Coverage of the nine Divine Nine graduate chapters is partial. Covered with a Philadelphia chapter: Alpha Phi Alpha (Rho), Alpha Kappa Alpha (Omega Omega), Kappa Alpha Psi (Philadelphia alumni), Omega Psi Phi (Zeta Iota Iota), Delta Sigma Theta (Philadelphia and Quaker City), Zeta Phi Beta (Beta Delta Zeta). Not confirmed in Philadelphia in this pass: Phi Beta Sigma, Iota Phi Theta, and Sigma Gamma Rho graduate chapters (only out of area found). Most chapters on the city partner list have no location checked and are in leads_only. National chapter finders could not be read: the AKA locator needs a city search form; the Sigma, Iota and SGR locators are interactive maps (the Iota and SGR map pages show no names in capture); the Kappa locator sits behind a members portal; the 100 Black Men national chapter list returned 404 and its find-a-chapter page is a map with no results in capture; the Links national chapter list returned 404; the Phi Beta Sigma regions page returned 404; alphaphialpha.org did not resolve. None of these was bypassed. Records rate membership chapters at newcomer 2 unless the site shows a clear public way in. Dates on several chapter sites have no year: Delta Philadelphia (October 15 event) and Quaker City (50th anniversary gala) years were inferred from the weekday or the anniversary and noted in each record. Community tags for the Divine Nine and Links chapters are limited to women or men because the pages read do not state a race rule. Jack and Jill is low confidence because its own pages returned 403. NCNW has no current Philadelphia section page or contact found, so it is a lead only. The 100 Black Men record notes a parent academy seen in search that was not confirmed.
